segments.text: Welcome to the daily Robotics digest for September 24th, 2026.
We're diving into world models, ROS evolution, and what's next at IROS 2026.
Here are seven stories for you.
From 🔳 Turing Post, "∇ Guide: How World Models Work – From Dreamer and JEPA to Waymo and Atlas"
details the mechanisms of world models and their application in systems like Waymo and Atlas.
These models are designed to capture how the physical world evolves following an agent's actions by predicting future states based on current observations and underlying dynamics.
Research explores various methodologies including visual-token models latent dynamics models such as Dreamer and JEPA and object-centric approaches.
The fundamental objective is to learn the governing dynamics that dictate transitions between different states in an environment.
This involves learning the relationships between observations and the resulting state changes through sophisticated modeling techniques.
The successful application of these methods facilitates more effective reasoning and interaction for artificial agents in physical settings.
Future developments in this area will focus on improving the accuracy and generalization of these predictive models.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Fifteen Years of MoveIt, and the Next Fifteen"
reports on a significant merger between PickNik Inc. and Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

This development is driven by the importance of the MoveIt project within robotics, highlighting the need for a hybrid approach combining artificial intelligence models with traditional MoveIt methods for reliable robotic deployment.
Qualcomm is acquiring PickNik to facilitate the integration of advanced artificial intelligence models directly onto physical hardware for real-time robot operation.
This strategic move addresses the requirement for integrating sophisticated AI capabilities with established motion planning frameworks.
The collaboration is positioned to continue supporting the open-source development of MoveIt and ROS.
This integration signifies a trajectory toward more robust and adaptable real-time robotic systems.
From Robohub, "What’s coming up at #IROS2026?".
This segment details the planned schedule and thematic focus for the upcoming IROS 2026 conference in Pittsburgh, USA.
The event will take place from September 27 to October 1 and will feature plenary talks, workshops, and forums.
Keynote speakers are scheduled to address diverse areas including autonomous surgery, embodied artificial intelligence, and soft robotics.
Community discussions will address topics such as United States government funding and robotics education.
Plenary panels are set to explore themes encompassing start-ups, space, and the role of robots as generalists or specialists, alongside numerous workshops and tutorials.
This event signifies a convergence of advanced robotics research and industry application.
The conference points toward future developments in autonomous systems and applied robotics research.
From Microsoft Research, "Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics"
reports on the benefits of moving AI inference to edge or cloud GPUs for physical robotics.
This offloading improves task success rates, allows for larger AI models, and enhances robot responsiveness in dynamic settings.
The research details that offloading physical AI inference to external GPUs provides substantial advantages over relying only on onboard robot processors.
This process results in improved task success rates and enables the use of larger AI models.
Furthermore, offloading significantly extends robot battery life by decreasing the power consumption required for onboard AI computation.

A new toolset utilizing Kubernetes facilitates the containerization and orchestration of these distributed robotics AI workloads, which is integrated into the Physical AI Toolchain for scalable, real-world deployment.
This development signals a path toward more efficient and capable physical AI systems in practical applications.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Announcement: rclrs 0.8.0 Release".
This announcement details the release of rclrs version zero point eight point zero, which supports ROS 2 Lyrical Luth bindings for multiple ROS 2 distributions.
The new release introduces the ability to access ROS message packages via the ros-env environment, which unifies message definitions across rclrs and applications.

Furthermore, the ActionClientState component now provides server availability information and supports parameter callbacks, alongside performance improvements and fixes in action handling and ROS initialization.
Applications utilizing generated messages are required to import them using the ros_env::*; directive.
This development streamlines message handling and improves interoperability within the ROS ecosystem.
The continued evolution of these bindings indicates a focus on enhancing the developer experience within robotic systems.
From Planet ROS, ROS Discourse General: ROSCon Global 2026 Live Stream.
This report covers the live stream of ROSCon Global 2026 currently broadcasting from Toronto.
The primary live stream is hosted on Vimeo in the Grand Ballroom West/Centre, with a secondary stream available later on Vimeo in the Grand Ballroom East after lunch.
The event features distinct posts corresponding to each participant within the discourse.

The live broadcast details indicate that the main session is being disseminated through the Grand Ballroom West/Centre stream, while an additional stream is scheduled for the Grand Ballroom East following the lunch period.
This structure allows for the comprehensive dissemination of all participant contributions from the conference.
The ongoing stream provides a direct view of the discussions taking place during the event.
Attention should be directed toward the continuing stream for updates on technological developments in the field.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROSCon Toronto FollowUp: Kubernetes/KubeEdge with ROS 2"
reports on discussions held at the recent ROSCon Toronto meetup concerning the integration of Kubernetes and KubeEdge with ROS 2.
The follow-up communication indicates that further detailed information regarding these technical discussions is available through an ongoing thread.
Discussions focused on the practical application and methodology of deploying ROS 2 systems within containerized and edge computing environments using Kubernetes.
The event facilitated sharing of practical implementations and exploration of the necessary frameworks for bridging the gap between robotics software and distributed systems infrastructure.
An online follow-up meeting is tentatively planned for October, with an invitation to be distributed upon the author's return to Tokyo.
This work points toward advancing the deployment strategies for real-time robotic systems across modern, distributed computing platforms.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your day runs as smoothly as a perfectly trained robot.
Go forth and ponder those world models!
See you tomorrow!
